title: Choose SafeDay's new visual world
question: Each direction removes the dashboard feel. Choose the world that should make planning outside feel immediate and human.

options.label: The Departure Board
options.lineage: rail departure boards and neighborhood timetables
options.thesis: Outdoor time becomes a departure you can catch, with one next window and a few later options.
options.viewport: A tiny place header, one monumental leave-time, an activity sentence, and a seven-day rail that reveals alternatives without opening a dashboard.
options.risk: Transit language can feel impersonal if the copy loses warmth.

raised.raise: The best time owns the viewport at poster scale while supporting facts stay quiet.
A changed condition is immediately visible in position and weight, never buried in copy.
Alternative days remain present as a physical stack instead of separate screens.
Changing the activity visibly reroutes the recommendation in one motion.

options.label: The Trail Marker
options.thesis: SafeDay acts like one clear marker at the start of an outing: go here, at this time, for this reason.
options.viewport: One route-like recommendation cuts through the screen, with the week folded into a compact trail legend below it.
options.risk: The familiar outdoor metaphor can become too literal if every control looks like signage.

options.label: The Daylight Horizon
options.lineage: stage cycloramas moving from night to day
options.thesis: The day is one changing horizon, and the recommendation sits where conditions open up.
options.viewport: A full-width daylight arc carries the selected window, with the person and activity anchored on the most favorable band.
options.case: It identifies with being outside, but the recommendation scans more slowly than the departure board.
options.risk: Color can become atmosphere instead of useful information.

options.label: The Lit Window
options.thesis: Only the next useful time is fully lit; the rest of the week stays as quiet ghost cells.
options.viewport: A near-black field holds one amber time at monumental scale, with later windows occupying fixed dim slots below.
options.case: It is exceptionally clear about time, but it feels less warm and relatable.
options.risk: The instrument language can feel severe for families and casual walkers.

options.label: The Gravity Garden
options.lineage: surreal gardens with local fields of gravity
options.thesis: Each activity bends the week toward a different good window.
options.viewport: A garden field reroutes weather toward the selected activity.
options.case: It is memorable, but the simulation competes with the simple planning task.
options.kept: Activity changes must visibly reroute the result.
options.risk: The concept could feel like a game rather than a trustworthy planner.

options.label: The Bitmap Specimen
options.thesis: One recommendation is typeset at poster scale and repeated through the week at smaller resolutions.
options.viewport: The chosen time towers above a specimen strip of alternative days.
options.case: It has typographic courage, but its editorial posture slows an everyday utility.
options.kept: The best time deserves overwhelming typographic priority.
options.risk: The page may read as a poster before it reads as a planner.

options.label: The Crisis Wall
options.thesis: Conditions become immediate system states around a monumental countdown.
options.viewport: A command wall frames the next window with alerts at the edges.
options.case: It communicates state strongly, but turns ordinary planning into an emergency.
options.kept: State changes should be spatially obvious.
options.risk: The alarm language conflicts with SafeDay's calm honesty.

options.label: The Exposure Record
options.lineage: darkroom exposure sheets and zone ramps
options.thesis: Each day is a translucent exposure sheet whose markings explain the recommendation.
options.viewport: Overlapping day sheets reveal the chosen window and conflicts beneath it.
options.case: It explains tradeoffs well, but adds expert-tool complexity to a consumer decision.
options.kept: Alternatives should remain physically present, not hidden behind navigation.
options.risk: Layered technical notation would raise cognitive load.

canonCard.label: The familiar weather app
canonCard.thesis: A polished forecast dashboard with a current card, hourly row, and seven daily cards.
canonCard.viewport: Location and search sit above a large current forecast card, then hourly and daily rows.
canonCard.risk: Easy to understand, but indistinguishable from the category by design.
